description: Security-relevant routing: guard coverage, path confusion, constraint bypass, priority surprises and reserved syntax
sources: README and docs/reference.md: Route patterns, Wildcards, Percent-encoding, Invalid patterns, Matching (Routes for any method, Trailing slashes and empty segments, Path normalization, Result ordering)
.agents/matching.md: Method-agnostic entries (the `methods[method] || methods[""]` fail-open), Empty segments and normalization
Orange Tsai, Breaking Parser Logic (Black Hat USA 2018): `;` and `..;/` path confusion between proxy and app

scenarios.name: admin area behind a method-agnostic `/admin/**` guard
scenarios.description: h3 `use()`-style auth on `/admin/**`, handlers at varied depth, a public catch-all page at the root. Every probe must hit the guard whenever an admin handler matches.

cases.note: a middle empty segment is real: no handler, but the guard still runs
%2F is never a separator
case-sensitive: the public page, never an admin handler
normalize resolves only literal dot segments
Cyrillic a

scenarios.name: the same scope guarded in every catch-all spelling
scenarios.description: Teams write the same auth scope as `**`, `*`, `**:rest`, `:rest*` and `:p(.*)`. All of them must cover the handlers below; their order on the shared node is `**` < `*` = `:p(.*)` < `**:name`.

cases.note: `**:rest` / `:rest*` need a value in every segment
static `x` wins over `:org`

scenarios.name: `:path*` guard skips paths with empty segments
scenarios.description: A dashboard guard written as `:path*` (URLPattern: every segment needs a value) does not cover a `*` file handler on paths with an empty segment. Write guards as `**` / `*`.

cases.note: documented: `:path*` takes no empty segment, so this guard is skipped

scenarios.name: numeric id constraint bypass attempts
scenarios.description: `:id(\d+)` must match a whole ASCII-digit segment only; anything else falls through to the `/users/**` middleware.

cases.note: raw newline: a `$` that matched before a final \n would let it through
fullwidth digits are not \d

scenarios.name: enum and mid-segment constraints are anchored per segment
scenarios.description: File extensions and formats allow-listed with alternations; a constraint must match its whole piece of the segment, never a prefix or suffix, and never across `/`.

cases.note: double extension: the last one is checked
`:file` needs a value
an unanchored `^csv|xlsx$` would accept it

scenarios.name: static self-service routes next to protected param routes
scenarios.description: `/users/me/*` is self-service, `/users/:id/*` is admin-only behind a guard. Static `me` wins, so `me` can never reach an admin handler, while the param guards still run on `me` paths.

cases.note: static `me` wins: the admin handler is never picked for `me`

scenarios.name: internal deny-all with a public health check
scenarios.description: Everything under `/internal` is denied for any method except `GET /internal/health`.

cases.note: HEAD is not mapped to GET

scenarios.name: method-specific deny loses to a more specific method-agnostic route
scenarios.description: `DELETE /api/**` reads like a deny-all for deletes, but specificity beats method: a deeper `""` route wins `findRoute`. Both stay in `findAllRoutes`.

scenarios.name: method-agnostic guard on the same node as a constrained handler (fail-open regression)
scenarios.description: A `""` guard must still match when the method's own entry on that node fails its constraint (never `methods[method] || methods[""]`). A constrained `""` entry outranks the method's plain one.

cases.note: the GET entry fails its regex: fall through to the `""` one
methods are not normalized: lowercase sees only `""` routes

scenarios.name: deny by default with GET allow-list
scenarios.description: A `""` `/**` deny-all, with a few GET routes allowed. Anything that misses the allow-list must land on the deny route, never on nothing.

scenarios.name: dotfile and source-map deny rules after a catch-all
scenarios.description: Static file server with `""` deny rules anchored at the end of the path (`/**/.env`, `/**/.git/config`, `/static/*.map`). From-end ranking makes the deny win wherever it matches.

cases.note: only one trailing slash is ignored: a file server that strips more must not trust this route
middle empty segment: not the deny route

scenarios.name: org scope with optional segments and a nested guard
scenarios.description: Tenant routes with an optional team segment and an optional invoice; the org guard and the billing guard must cover every variant.

scenarios.name: versioned API admin guard with a static legacy route
scenarios.description: The admin guard is written with a `:version` param; a constrained and a static legacy handler sit under it next to an API-wide 404 catch-all.

scenarios.name: `/api/*` scope covers the scope root
scenarios.description: README `use("/api/*")`: a trailing `*` is optional, so the guard covers `/api` and `/api/` too; extra slashes stay inside its capture.

scenarios.name: method handling around a guarded scope
scenarios.description: Method strings are not normalized: lowercase or unknown methods see only `""` routes; a method-specific deny ties a `""` guard on its node and wins `findRoute`.

scenarios.name: percent-encoding and lookalike characters
scenarios.description: Literal pattern text is encoded once at insert; lookup paths are never decoded, so encoded, lowercase-hex, NFD and lookalike spellings never reach a route.

cases.note: Cyrillic a

scenarios.name: deep and long paths
scenarios.description: A root deny-all guard over deep static, many-param and catch-all-with-suffix routes; long segments and long paths must neither match wrongly nor escape the guard.

scenarios.name: constraint footguns: unescaped dot and constraints that could span segments
scenarios.description: An unescaped `.` in a constraint matches any character; `(.+)` / `([^.]*)` stay within their segment in the router while `routeToRegExp` spans segments (over-match, never under-match).

cases.note: the `.` in the constraint is unescaped
`(.+)` stays within its segment
a constraint may take an empty segment

scenarios.name: edit actions guarded from the end of the path
scenarios.description: `"" /**/edit` guards edit actions at any depth; segments after a catch-all match from the end and outrank a plain catch-all viewer.

scenarios.name: optional locale prefix on a guarded account area
scenarios.description: Both the guard and the handler start with a leading `{/:lang}?` group; every locale variant must stay covered.

cases.note: `:tab?` also registers `/account/profile`: registration order decides (docs/reference.md carve-out)

scenarios.name: extension guard written with a `*` inside a segment
scenarios.description: `"" /api/*.json` guards every JSON endpoint at any depth below `/api` (the `*` spans segments); named handlers must stay covered and win where they match.

scenarios.name: tenant admin guard with a `*` before more of the route
scenarios.description: `"" /tenants/*/admin` matches `admin` under any tenant path (the `*` takes one segment or more, from the end); handlers with params must stay covered.

scenarios.name: plausible patterns that must throw
scenarios.description: Patterns a developer might write for an auth rule that would otherwise silently match something unexpected.
